name: Parabola Independence
description: You are given a set of $$$n$$$ quadratic functions $$$F=\{f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_n \}$$$, where $$$f_i(x)=a_i x^2 + b_i x + c_i$$$. Two functions $$$f$$$ and $$$g$$$ are called independent if $$$f(x) \neq g(x)$$$ for all $$$x \in \mathbb{R}$$$. Also, a set of functions $$$G=\{g_1,g_2,\ldots,g_k\}$$$ is called organized if the two functions $$$g_i$$$ and $$$g_j$$$ are independent for all $$$1 \le i \lt j \le |G|$$$. For each $$$i=1,2,\ldots,n$$$, please find the size of the largest organized subset of $$$F$$$ that contains $$$f_i$$$ as an element.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 3000$$$). Each of the $$$n$$$ following lines contains three integers $$$a_i$$$, $$$b_i$$$, $$$c_i$$$ denoting the function $$$f_i$$$ ($$$-10^6 \le a_i, b_i, c_i \le 10^6$$$, $$$a_i \neq 0$$$). It is guaranteed that the functions in one test case are pairwise distinct. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n^2$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$3000^2$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output $$$n$$$ integers $$$s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_n$$$, where $$$s_i$$$ is the size of the largest organized subset that contains $$$f_i$$$.
approach_summary: Apply Knapsack and Basic Dynamic Programming paradigm under the Dynamic Programming (DP) framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
